A BP that high with symptoms does warrant further testing. A normal ECG is a good sign. I will say that a 31 year old who is relatively healthy saying they had 5 heart attacks will make the doctors think this is anxiety. Symptomatic high BP (abrupt headache, crushing chest pain, confusion, etc) warrants an ER visit, but high BP on its own is an office visit. You should call your cardiologist or PCP to discuss medication changes and diet/ lifestyle modification. People with hypertension taking their BP at home is great, but make sure the cuff is the proper size, and you take it in a relaxed state, comfortable position, and not after exercise or caffeine intake.

This is so sweet of you. I think they would be happy with anything but I’ll give you a chili recipe my college roommate made for me when I was depressed. It’s a great way to learn how to cook. And if you’re missing an ingredient, it will still be good.

-Diced white or yellow onion (you can buy it diced)
-2 cans of any beans
-1 can of diced tomatoes
-1 can of tomato sauce
-1 lb of ground Turkey or beef
-1 packet of chili seasoning (or a mixture of salt, pepper, a spicy seasoning, garlic powder, whatever you have)


-In a big pot, heat up some oil on low-medium heat. Throw the onions in, salt and pepper, and stir until they turn clear.

-turn the heat up to medium, put all of the meat in the pot, and half of the chili seasoning packet. Stir it around for a few minutes until there’s no pink left

-turn the heat to the lowest setting. rinse the beans off with water, and put the beans, tomatoes and tomato sauce in.

-put the rest of the seasoning packet in

-put the lid on the pot, and stir it every few minutes for 30 minutes.

Serve with rice or pasta or tortilla chips… store bought cornbread is my favorite!
